broker.description: TOOLS_VAULT_BROKER -- the ONE sender this vault answers. It is a capability broker's `invoke` cell, and there is none in this hive: that is the decision that has to be made before this occupant is wired.

description.purpose: A secret store with no operation that returns a secret, standing in this hive as an occupant rather than as a peer -- so that a colony which does want one behind the tool door has a directory to wake instead of a template to copy.
description.use_when: NOT WIRED IN THE SHIPPED TREE. A vault answers exactly ONE sender, its broker, and attests its own inbound edges before it accepts key material: wired here with no broker beside it, it would attest `broker_unwired` and stay locked on every call. The shipped arrangement is the other one -- a vault stands in the capability broker's hive, next to the `invoke` cell that is allowed to spend it.
description.not_in_scope: No read operation, in any topology: `put`, `rotate`, `use`, `revoke`, `status`, `unlock`, `lock` and `deliver` are the whole surface and none of them hands a secret back. No key material in this tree either -- what is written down is the NAME of a source, never a value.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one tool_result turn per operation. hop.error_code carries the refusal -- `access_denied` for a sender that is not the broker, `attestation_failed` for a neighbourhood it does not recognise, `vault_locked` for a vault whose key never arrived.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: a tool_call turn whose text is JSON args {op, name, ...}.
examples: left as shipped -> an island: no edge names it, the boot registers it inactive, nothing reaches it
wired without a broker in the same hive -> every call comes back `attestation_failed`, which is the refusal working, not the cell failing
